 Home Alex Pereira Henry Cejudo Alex Pereira given a reality check about his ‘spoiled’ heavyweight complaints by ex-UFC double champ
 Harvey Leonard Thu 15 October 2026 21:00 Follow us on Google Discover It is safe to say that Henry Cejudo does not have much sympathy for ‘Poatan’. 
 Alex Pereira has not shied away from expressing his frustrations with the UFC publicly since a defeat on the White House lawn this past June.
 After missing out on making history as the first three-division champion at UFC Freedom 250, where Pereira was knocked out by Ciryl Gane , the Brazilian fan favorite began a campaign against referee Herb Dean.
 More recently, Pereira has complained about the decision to have Josh Hokit challenge Gane instead of him. But ‘Poatan’ does not have the support of a fellow former UFC double champ in that regard.
 LATEST NEWS: Six-time UFC headliner signs with surprise new promotion 20 months after his last fight 
 How much has your opinion of Alex Pereira changed since his UFC Freedom 250 loss?
 Has Alex Pereira lost his aura since UFC Freedom 250? Credit: Ed Mulholland/Zuffa LLC Comment Like or Comment Have your say Sign-in now for free Henry Cejudo tells Alex Pereira he has ‘skipped the line’ enough amid his UFC complaints
 Some have begun to change their opinions of the ex-light heavyweight and middleweight after some of his remarks.
 Pereira called out Daniel Cormier earlier this week, accusing the former champion-turned-color commentator of pushing an agenda that made the UFC book Gane vs Hokit.
 Reacting to that claim, Dana White called Pereira “paranoid,” and it would seem many of the Brazilian’s own supporters agree with that assessment.
 The latest to give their take was Cejudo , another big name in the club of two-division title winners on MMA’s biggest stage.
 ‘Triple C’ shut down Pereira’s complaints, reminding him of the privileged positions he has already been given by the UFC.
 “This is something that I will say about Alex Pereira, and it’s part of him being a bit spoiled,” Cejudo said during a recent episode of his Pound 4 Pound podcast alongside Kamaru Usman.
 “Alex, I’m not picking on you. I’m just seeing what has been done with you, and how is it that you’ve skipped lines. You’ve skipped the line long enough, bro.
 “You had your opportunity against Ciryl Gane, and you lost,” he continued. “Yeah, there were illegal blows, I agree with you on that. But that jab from Gane wobbled you.
 “It was your debut at heavyweight. It is what it is. To be upset after not having a fight at heavyweight and then getting a shot to fight for the interim title at the White House?! Bro, there’s no complaining.
 “I feel like he needed to win at least two or three more to fight for the title.”
 LATEST NEWS: Josh Hokit responds after being told to ‘show some class’ by UFC announcer Bruce Buffer 
 Photo by Jeff Bottari/Zuffa LLC While ‘The Incredible Hok’ has his chance to make Gane’s undisputed title reign a short one, ‘Poatan’ will be looking to secure his spot opposite the winner in 2027.
 A month after the UFC 334 heavyweight title fight, Pereira will face Sergei Pavlovich in his second appearance in the division.
